summary: EU-West: ~20–30% tokens/sec drop on rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct after model version update (Dedicated)
description:
Customer-reported throughput regression (tokens/sec) in eu-west immediately following a Redwood catalog model version update for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct.

Issue summary
- Customer: KestrelPay (Dedicated)
- Region: eu-west
- Model: rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct
- Regression: ~20–30% lower decode throughput (tokens/sec) vs prior week, observed in customer-side instrumentation and Redwood Console.
- Start time: 2026-02-10 ~08:40 UTC (customer noticed ~09:15 UTC)
- Customer impact: request duration increased for long-form generations; downstream queueing on their side during peak.

Customer report (from email / support portal)
- "We updated to the latest model version for llama-3.1-70b-instruct in eu-west and immediately saw tokens/sec drop from ~105 tok/s to ~75–85 tok/s at similar concurrency. Latency increased but mostly driven by slower generation. No increase in 5xx. Can we roll back or pin the previous version?"

Environment / workload notes
- Dedicated cluster in eu-west (GPU SKU reported by customer: A100 80GB).
- Workload characteristics (customer provided):
  - prompt_tokens: ~800–2,000
  - output_tokens: ~400–1,200
  - streaming: mixed (their app uses streaming for ~60% of calls)
  - concurrency: 8–20 in-flight per pod

Initial investigation (Support)
1) Confirmed model version change in eu-west around 08:35–08:45 UTC via deploy annotations.
2) Compared perf-canary slices for the same model/region to separate platform-wide regression vs customer-specific workload effect.
3) Checked whether regression is isolated to GPU SKU and/or scheduler mode.

Findings (Perf Canary + internal dashboards)
- Perf-canary showed a matching decode throughput drop on eu-west for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct on A100 slices starting at the same deploy annotation.
- H100 slice did not show a comparable drop.
- Kernel selection export for canary-tagged requests indicates increased kernel fallback rate on A100 for long decode sequences after the model version update (fallback reason: "unsupported epilogue for int4 path" seen in sample logs).
- Scheduler mode pinned for canary was stable; customer cluster uses default scheduler mode. However, the regression reproduced in canary under pinned scheduler, suggesting it is not primarily scheduling variance.

Hypothesis
- The eu-west catalog update switched the default variant for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct to a new quantized artifact on A100 (or changed quantization/kernel compatibility), causing kernel fallback and reduced decode throughput.

Mitigation options shared with customer
- Immediate mitigation: pin model version back to previous known-good build (available via model version pin) while we roll back the eu-west default.
- Alternative: switch to the fp16 (non-quantized) variant for A100 until kernels support the new artifact without fallback.
- If customer requires latest weights: reduce max_output_tokens temporarily to limit tail amplification, or separate long-form traffic to a dedicated route.

Resolution
- Rolled back eu-west default for rw-llama-3.1-70b-instruct to previous catalog version at 2026-02-10 18:20 UTC.
- Verified perf-canary tokens/sec returned to baseline band within 30–45 minutes post-roll-back (after warmup/cache priming).
- Customer confirmed throughput recovered by 2026-02-11 09:05 UTC.

Follow-ups
- Runtime to add/validate kernel support for the new quantized artifact on A100; ensure catalog rollout gates on perf-canary A100 slice.
- Telemetry: add explicit model_variant label (coarse) in perf-canary views to avoid ambiguity on artifact changes without exploding cardinality.
- Support: add a saved response + checklist for "throughput regression after model update" including perf-canary comparison links and model pin instructions.
